subject.title: fix(gateway): bound connect frame auth.* fields at the protocol schema

question: Should connect-frame auth fields be bounded by UTF-8 byte length, by explicit ASCII token shape, or is the current grapheme-count `maxLength` acceptable for this pre-auth security boundary?
rationale: The choice affects both the DoS mitigation and compatibility for shared-secret/runtime-token clients, so the permanent protocol contract needs gateway/security owner acceptance rather than an implicit schema-only decision.

options.title: Require byte or token-shape bounds
options.body: Block merge until the schema or handshake boundary rejects oversized byte payloads, or restricts affected token fields to ASCII formats where length matches byte cost.

options.title: Accept grapheme caps as-is
options.body: Merge the current shape knowing it still permits high-byte single-grapheme payloads within the pre-auth frame limit and may leave the stated amplification gap partially open.

options.title: Narrow the cap surface
options.body: Cap only the machine-generated bootstrap/device paths now and defer shared/runtime token policy to a follow-up protocol decision.

recommendation.title: Require byte or token-shape bounds
recommendation.body: Block merge until the schema or handshake boundary rejects oversized byte payloads, or restricts affected token fields to ASCII formats where length matches byte cost.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent schema extraction history and merger role on adjacent gateway auth hardening make this the best available owner for the protocol/security-boundary choice.
